Action Plan:
1. Provide patient with NHS self-referral link for evidence-based talking therapy (CBT) to address work-related anxiety.  
2. Email/attach reputable online resources for immediate anxiety-management and sleep-hygiene techniques.  
3. Arrange baseline blood tests (FBC, TFTs, U&E, glucose) to exclude metabolic contributors to palpitations; patient to phone support line to book phlebotomy.  
4. Schedule GP review 1 week after blood tests to discuss results and re-assess anxiety, sleep, and palpitations.  
5. Advise patient to seek earlier review if anxiety escalates, palpitations become persistent/prolonged, chest pain occurs, or work/social functioning deteriorates.  
6. Lifestyle advice: gradual return to exercise, limit caffeine/chocolate, moderate alcohol, avoid smoking.  
7. Document sleep-hygiene tips within after-visit summary.  
8. Discussed that pharmacotherapy is not indicated at this stage but may be considered if non-pharmacological measures insufficient.  
9. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaints (2 months): escalating morning anxiety about work; palpitations; insomnia (sleep 3–4 h/night); low energy; loss of enjoyment; social and activity avoidance.  
• Onset/progression: Began shortly after starting new, stressful head-office job in fashion retail; symptoms worsening.  
• Palpitations: irregular fast heartbeat, mainly on waking, lasting minutes (up to 10 min); no associated chest pain except awareness of rapid beat.  
• Mood: persistent low mood/anhedonia but denies suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.  
• Appetite: largely unchanged; increased chocolate intake.  
• Past medical history: none reported.  
• Medications: none reported.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Social: Lives with parents; full-time employment; alcohol—heavy on Fri/Sat plus occasional weekday wine; occasional smoker; no recreational drugs.  
• Family history: Mother has history of depression.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed during remote consult.  
• No vitals available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Generalised work-related anxiety
   - Assessment: Probable Generalised Anxiety Disorder precipitated by new job stress.
   - Investigations planned: None specific (see palpitations).
   - Treatment planned: Self-referral to NHS Talking Therapies (CBT); online anxiety resources; lifestyle modification; safety-netting.  
   - Relevant referrals: Psychological therapy services (self-referral link provided).

2. Palpitations
   - Assessment: Likely anxiety-induced palpitations.
   - Differential diagnosis: Thyroid dysfunction, anaemia, arrhythmia.
   - Investigations planned: Baseline blood tests (FBC, TFTs, U&E, random glucose); consider ECG if symptoms persist or abnormal blood results.
   - Treatment planned: Control underlying anxiety; monitor frequency/severity; urgent review if chest pain, syncope, or prolonged episodes.

3. Insomnia / Sleep disturbance
   - Assessment: Secondary to anxiety and job stress.
   - Treatment planned: Sleep-hygiene education (regular bedtime, screen avoidance, relaxation techniques); resume moderate exercise; limit alcohol/caffeine; follow-up at next review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: allergy status, current medication reconciliation, vital signs, physical/mental state examination findings.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient described palpitations as “irregular” yet concerned they may be “fast”; no further clarification (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear speech; minor inaudible clinician affirmations; clinically sufficient.
